questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: Mango, Banana, Guava, Tomato, Papaya
questions.explanation: C is correct. Mango, Banana, Guava, and Papaya are all fruits (botanically and in common culinary usage). Tomato is botanically a fruit but in Indian cuisine and everyday classification is treated as a vegetable. In SSC reasoning, Tomato is the odd one out as it doesn't belong with 'fruits used in everyday eating'. Trap: Guava and Banana are also unique in texture/form but all are categorised as fruits in common parlance.

C is correct. 17, 23, 29, and 41 are all prime numbers. 35 = 5×7 is composite (not prime). All appear to follow an AP with d=6 but that's a distractor — the key property is primeness. 35 is the odd one out. Trap: looks like an AP (each differs by 6) but the primeness property separates 35.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: Violin, Guitar, Sitar, Tabla, Veena
questions.explanation: D is correct. Violin, Guitar, Sitar, and Veena are all stringed instruments (chordophones — played by plucking or bowing strings). Tabla is a percussion instrument (membranophone — played by striking a membrane). Tabla is the odd one out. Trap: all may seem 'Indian instruments' but Violin and Guitar are also included, confirming the unifying property is 'stringed instruments' not 'Indian origin'.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out based on the internal pattern: ACE, BDF, CGI, EGI
questions.explanation: C is correct. Check gaps between letters (positions in alphabet): ACE: A(1)→C(3)=+2, C(3)→E(5)=+2. Equal gaps ✓. BDF: B(2)→D(4)=+2, D(4)→F(6)=+2. Equal gaps ✓. CGI: C(3)→G(7)=+4, G(7)→I(9)=+2. Unequal gaps ✗ (should be C,E,G for equal +2 gaps). EGI: E(5)→G(7)=+2, G(7)→I(9)=+2. Equal gaps ✓. CGI is the odd one out — its first gap (+4) breaks the +2,+2 pattern. Trap: EGI shares letters with CGI but has equal gaps; C→G skips D,E,F (4 steps) instead of 2.

C is correct. 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³, 64 = 4³, 125 = 5³ are all perfect cubes. 100 = 10² is a perfect square but NOT a perfect cube. 100 is the odd one out. Trap: 64 = 4³ but also 8² (perfect square) — the defining property here is CUBES, and 100 fails this test.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, Teacher, Hospital
questions.explanation: D is correct. Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, and Teacher are all professions (designations of people). Hospital is a place — not a profession. It does not belong with the others. Trap: one might associate 'Doctor' with 'Hospital' but Doctor remains a profession, not a place.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: Km, Litre, Metre, Mile, Centimetre
questions.explanation: B is correct. Km, Metre, Mile, and Centimetre are all units of length/distance. Litre is a unit of volume (capacity), not length. Litre is the odd one out. Trap: Mile is an Imperial unit while the others are mostly metric — but Mile is still a unit of length, so it belongs with the group.

D is correct. 144 = 12², 169 = 13², 196 = 14², 225 = 15² are all perfect squares. 228 is not a perfect square (√228 ≈ 15.1). 228 is the odd one out. Trap: 169 might seem odd (13 is prime) but it is still a perfect square.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: January, March, May, July, August
questions.explanation: D is correct. January, March, May, and July are months with 31 days that appear in the sequence of 'every other odd month' (months 1, 3, 5, 7). August (month 8) is an even-numbered month — it doesn't fit the pattern of odd-numbered months. The group January(1), March(3), May(5), July(7) are all odd-numbered months with 31 days. August is the 8th month (even). Trap: All 5 months have 31 days, which is the surface-level common property — but the deeper pattern is odd-numbered months, excluding August.

questions.stem: Choose the odd one out: BEH, CFI, DGJ, EHL, FIL
questions.explanation: C is correct. Check gaps in each group: BEH: B(2)→E(5)=+3, E(5)→H(8)=+3 ✓. CFI: C(3)→F(6)=+3, F(6)→I(9)=+3 ✓. DGJ: D(4)→G(7)=+3, G(7)→J(10)=+3 ✓. EHL: E(5)→H(8)=+3, H(8)→L(12)=+4 ✗ (should be +3, giving K=11, not L=12). FIL: F(6)→I(9)=+3, I(9)→L(12)=+3 ✓. EHL breaks the +3,+3 pattern — its third letter should be K (H+3=11=K), not L. EHL is the odd one out. Trap: FIL looks suspicious since L(12)=I(9)+3 ✓ is correct.
